title: FBI Crime Database Reportedly Hacked: 18 Million Records. What We Actually Know.
summary: The FBI's National Crime Information Center has reportedly been breached. The FBI has not publicly said what, if anything, was stolen or changed.

title: Jensen Huang Resigned. Days Later Nvidia Reported $115.8 Billion: Should He Return?
summary: Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue, up 103%, five days after announcing CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. Should he return?

title: Ohio's $1.57 Billion Tax Break: Who Pays for AI's Water and Power?
summary: Ohio's tax department says one data-centre tax break cost the state about $1.57 billion in 2025, against a state forecast of $136 million. Who pays for the power and water AI data centres use?

title: Jeffries Wins Speaker Nomination 251-11. Who Said No?
summary: House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries for speaker 251-11 in a closed-door caucus vote on 18 Nov 2026. Reported, not settled.

title: Epstein Files: Congress Voted 427 to 1. What Is Still Disputed?
summary: One year ago, the House voted 427 to 1 to release the Epstein files. What the Justice Department says, what a House Oversight report says, and what is still disputed.

title: Netanyahu's Candidate Loses 66–52. Now His Office Faces Questions.
summary: Israel's Knesset elected opposition MK Matan Kahana as speaker, 66 to 52. A Channel 12 report makes allegations about the prime minister's office, which denies wrongdoing.

title: GTA 6 Launches Thursday: Games, Kids and the Records Nobody Reads
summary: GTA 6 launches Thursday 19 November 2026 and is rated R18+ in Australia. What do the records say about children and games? Every allegation is attributed.

title: Vote Chori: 2 Crore Names Omitted From Maharashtra's Draft Voter List
summary: Maharashtra's draft voter list omitted 2,06,88,487 electors after the Special Intensive Revision. The Election Commission disputes the allegation of vote theft.

title: The Alexander Brothers: How One Australian’s Lawsuit Led to 30 Years Each
summary: Three brothers were each sentenced to 30 years in a US federal court. This video covers the lawsuits, the arrests, the trial, the verdict, the sentence and the pardon question. The brothers maintain their innocence.

title: Tinder, Hinge, Bumble, Grindr: Who Really Owns Your Dating Data?
summary: Follows the documents on who owns the big dating apps, what data they collect, and whether any of it has been used to trap people. Different levels of evidence are kept apart.

title: India Blocked 129 Websites on Two Fake Court Orders
summary: Reuters found that India's telecoms department ordered 129 betting websites blocked using two forged High Court orders. Who created the documents is still unknown.
